report.source_text: The cystic mass measured 5 cm in diameter and its content was completely removed after the surgical field was isolated with gauze impregnated with hypertonic solution (NaCl 10%). The cystic mass found was an echinococcal cyst with several daughter cysts measuring up to 10 mm within it. After removal of the daughter cysts and a partial resection of the pericyst, no involvement/penetration of the heart wall was found (Fig. 4). The remained cavity of the cyst was washed out with hypertonic solution (NaCl 10%) and left open.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-year-old man presented with chronic dry cough, chest pain, fatigue, low grade fever, and night sweats. Initial chest X-ray showed mediastinal enlargement and left pleural effusion. A Chest CT scan revealed a walled cystic mass (56x50mm) near the upper left atrium, ascending aorta, and pulmonary artery, compatible with a hydatid cyst, along with a 10mm endoatrial filling defect. Serological tests for echinococcosis were negative. Surgical removal of the mass confirmed it to be an echinococcal cyst with several daughter cysts (up to 10mm), with no heart wall involvement. Postoperatively, the patient recovered well and was discharged, receiving three courses of albendazole.
